metric.name: frame_p95_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur, a.jank_type
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  frames AS (
    SELECT * FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT dur AS ns, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY dur) AS rank, count(*) OVER () AS n
    FROM frames
  )
SELECT (SELECT ns / 1e6 FROM ranked WHERE rank = (n * 95 + 99) / 100) AS value

claims.text: The selected frame-duration p95 improved from 81.499417 ms in the baseline to 72.295959 ms in the current trace, a delta of -9.203458 ms; this is not a performance regression.

claims.text: The range's final commit changes the TV controls hide timeout from five seconds to four seconds in TvScreen.kt; it does not provide evidence of a frame-performance regression.
The changed timeout constant is attributed by blame to commit 82cde0d4acda1b40a0044ed8a118b168410d3aee, but the trace metrics improved rather than regressed, so no culprit is assigned.

caveats: This diagnosis compares one capture per side, so ordinary run-to-run variability cannot be ruled out.
The captures were made on an emulator, which can add timing variability.
